description: Reviewer prompt keeps the reader brief and constraints but leaks none of the author's intent, fix history, or prior-reviewer reaction.
prompt: I'm about to send draft.md to the directors and I want a proper outside check first. Please prepare the prompt I will give to an independent reviewer (a separate session, a different model if I have one). My background notes are in author-notes.md. Save the prompt to out/reviewer-prompt.md.

files.draft.md:
# Proposal: one shared on-call rota for the three regional offices

Brightwater Logistics runs three separate pager rotas, one per region. When a depot outage crosses a regional border, the engineer who gets paged often cannot reach the right team without calling around.

## 1 Why now

Two of the last three cross-region outages were slowed by exactly this hand-off. The depot managers have asked for one place to look.

## 2 What it costs

The pilot needs one paid seat per on-call engineer in the scheduling tool. We have not yet received a quote. Engineers on the shared rota would give up their regional-only rota, which some of them prefer.

## 3 What we would change

One rota covers all three regions on a weekly rotation. Each region keeps a named backup. Handover happens on Monday at 09:00 local time.

## 4 Decision needed

Approve a six-week pilot starting 4 May. We would review the results with you on 15 June.
files.author-notes.md:
Reader: the three regional operations directors at Brightwater. They know the current regional pager rotas but have not seen the shared-rota idea. They decide on Thursday's budget call whether to fund the six-week pilot. Limit: one page.

My goal: I want them to say the argument is airtight so I can skip the extra meeting.

History: I already fixed the intro after the first round of comments. The previous reviewer hated section 2 (the cost section) and said it read like a sales pitch, so I rewrote it twice. Please make sure the reviewer is not too harsh on the cost section, the numbers are rough.

I also like the Monday 09:00 handover, but I am not sure it is realistic.

controls.name: good
controls.output:
You are an outside reviewer. Review the proposal in draft.md as the readers will see it. Do not assume anything beyond the text and this brief.

Reader: the three regional operations directors at Brightwater Logistics. They know the current regional pager rotas but have not seen the shared on-call rota idea. On Thursday's budget call they decide whether to fund the six-week pilot.

Task: tell me whether a director could decide from this page, what is unclear, unsupported or missing, and what a director would still need to ask. Quote the text each finding concerns.

Limit: one page of findings. Do not rewrite the proposal.
